parts.text: From Source 1, how many cities monitor air pollution?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: From Source 2, identify two advantages of using electric vehicles.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Which advantage of using electric vehicles do you think is the most significant? Explain why.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why the problems of pollution from transport are an important local issue.

text: Study Sources 1 to 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘We need less polluting forms of transport for the future.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Cycling and walking are becoming more popular in cities.’
How could you test this claim?
You should consider the types of information, sources of evidence or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one opinion from Bina’s statement. Explain why it is an opinion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Ahram is arguing that we should find less polluting ways to travel.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify one fact from Ahram’s statement.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain how well this fact supports Ahram’s statement.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Bina’s or Ahram’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A government wants to reduce pollution in its cities.
The following actions are being considered:
• promoting the use of electric vehicles
• encouraging more walking and cycling
• making public transport free.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
